description:

https://github.com/every-app/every-app

Every App standardizes how to build apps using Cloudflare. It makes it easy to share what you've built and self host. You can self host hundreds of apps on their $5/month plan. People just need to build them!
At this hack, you have lots of options:
- Build an "Open source alternative to X"

title: Sundai Hack 132- On-device AI - 19 Jul
description:
Join us for hack #132!
Two months ago, running a useful LLM meant an API key and someone else's datacenter. This week, a 27B model runs on an iPhone.
The on-device world just crossed a threshold. Liquid AI’s LFM2.5-8B-A1B is built for private local agents. It can chain tool calls, stays below 6 GB on laptops, and runs at around 30 tokens per second on a phone. Gemma 4 ships Apache 2.0 variants that run on everything from a Raspberry Pi to a workstation, with vision and audio built in. Qwen 3.6 scores in frontier territory on real software engineering benchmarks while fitting on a single consumer GPU. And PrismML just open-sourced a 1-bit compressed Qwen 3.6 27B that squeezes 54 GB of weights into under 4 GB, small enough to run fully local on a phone, with every parameter active.
The catch: nobody actually knows what these models can do yet. This Sundai is about showing to the world what comes next.
Some ideas to hack on:
1. Stress-test the new generation. Drop Gemma 4 or Qwen 3.6 into real agentic harnesses like Claude Code and OpenClaw. Where do they hold up against cloud models, and where do they fall apart?
2. Build local-first apps. Voice assistants, RAG over your own files, coding agents, camera-in-the-loop tools. If it works with internet off, it counts double.
3. Go small or go weird. Run a model on a phone, a Pi, a browser tab. Build your own harness. Find the smallest model that can still complete your task.
Bring a laptop. One ollama pull and you have a frontier-adjacent model on your machine with no token meter running.
The frontier isn't only in the datacenter anymore. This sunday you can find out how much of it fits in your pocket.
Come join and hack with MediaLab experts!

title: Sundai Hack 131 - World Models - 12 Jul
description:
Join us for a Sundai Hack on world models! We’ll experiment with models that simulate environments, answer “what if?” questions, and help agents make smarter decisions.
No prior experience with world models is required - just curiosity and a willingness to learn and experiment. 
Example Projects You Could Build:
- A scalable world model that improves long‑horizon generation and planning stability.
- A world model that enables counterfactual reasoning and “what‑if” analysis eg. using a learned world model to simulate alternative actions or interventions and compare predicted outcomes.
- A world model trained on real‑world data (e.g., traffic, systems telemetry, or robotics) to simulate future system behavior under different conditions.
- Combining vision, actions, and language in a single world model eg. predicting how textual instructions affect future visual states.
These are just examples - unexpected, ambitious, and original project ideas are strongly encouraged. Come learn, build, and explore the future of intelligent systems!

title: Agent Harness Hack - 17 May
description:
Join us for a hack on building and customizing AI agent harnesses — the runtime layer that makes your agents actually useful.

In this hack, we'll explore what becomes possible when you build or customize your own. 
Whether you want to automate code reviews, run an autonomous company, orchestrate multi-step workflows, or just make your existing agent setup smarter — a custom harness is how you can get there.

title: Sundai - Climate AI Hack - Google AlphaEarth
description:

- Woodwell and Woods Hole scientific community form a world center for marine,
biomedical, and environmental scientific exploration

- Woodwell was established in 1985, making it one of the first organizations in the world dedicated to fighting climate change

title: Sundai - 18 May - Manolis Kellis, "Mantis AI"
description:
This Sundai we will hack on Mantis, an AI-powered Visual Data Science platform developed by Manolis Kellis and his team at MIT. 
As AI is reshaping how we work, reason, and learn, current chatbot frameworks are unfortunately excluding humans from the creative process, underutilizing the extraordinary acuity of human visual cognition, hiding away necessary complexity, and providing over-confident and over-simplified answers to complex questions, resulting in reduced human creativity and ingenuity.
Mantis provides a new paradigm for human-AI collaboration that extends human conceptual reach, insight, and speed, by blending natural language, structured data, and visual reasoning into an interactive canvas for exploration and discovery. User interactions are enriched with a wide range of tools and capabilities, including: lasso selection, magic lasso, bags, paths, partitions, clusters, ontologies, flashcards, waypoints, vignettes, journeys, quick-sheets, keywords, plotting, coding, notebooks, collaboration, and a crew of interactive, interacting, reasoning, learning expert agents, and their coordinating orchestrator.    
Mantis is based on Cognitive Cartography, Agentic Workflows, Multi-Modal Embeddings, and Contextual Reasoning.
The Mantis platform can be applied to almost any "vertical", from knowledge management, to business analytics, investment portfolios, startups, founders, patents, publications, genes, drugs, patients, products, buyers, sellers, ideas, songs, meetings, people, financial reports, government documents, laws, regulations, code, GitHub commits, progress reports, memos, news, books, historical events, Wikipedia, social media, YouTube videos, and education. 
The goal of our hack will be to build on top of the Mantis platform: (1) select a vertical; (2) gather/scrape relevant dataset; (3) decide on capabilities, questions, protocols, and agentic workflows; (4) navigate complex information space of your data to discover new insights
